note: Nauru, read on 2026-10-30 in RONLAW (ronlaw.gov.nr, the Republic's online legal database): the Immigration Regulations 2014 in their Service 6 consolidation (pages dated 15 October 2026, taking in Act 21 of 2026, in force 12 May 2026, and SL 20 of 2026, in force 30 April 2026), read through RONLAW's own search service, whose indexed page text was saved (the site shows its PDFs in a script viewer). Fees are in Australian dollars, Nauru's currency. Regulation 4 lists the classes: business, dependant's, local business (employment), regional processing centre, residence, special purpose, visitor's and temporary settlement visas; the regional processing centre and temporary settlement visas (asylum seekers and refugees) and the special purpose and visitor's visas aren't residence routes and aren't written. Business visa (Employment), for engaging in employment in Nauru (reg 6(2)), holds on the condition that its holder engage in no employment other than that specified in the visa without the Secretary's written permission (reg 6(4)(g)), so its work is the sponsor's; its fee in Schedule 2's Table 1 is $6,000, the only figure its row gives (the table's two columns are multiple entry up to 12 months and single entry up to 3 months; which column the figure stands in isn't read). Business visa (General), to conduct a business or profession, is self-employed: $6,000 for multiple entry up to 12 months (written), $3,000 for a single entry up to 3 months (not written). A business visa is granted for a period not exceeding 12 months (reg 6(5)), a most, not a term, so no term is written; Part 3 adds a non-refundable $50 processing fee to every business visa (not summed into the fee). The local business (employment) visa is for a foreign national employed by a Nauruan employer (a citizen or a wholly Nauruan-owned business) where no skilled Nauruans are available, a qualification is required by law, or the work is necessary to provide goods and services (reg 8(1)); it must be obtained before entering Nauru (reg 8(8), written as applied for abroad), authorises its holder to reside and work only for the employer named and the work of the contract (reg 8(9)), is granted for not more than 12 months (no term written), and costs $300 for a single person ($400 for a spouse and children, not written), its fee never waived. The residence visa may only be granted to a dependant of a Nauruan citizen (reg 10(1)), applied for before, on or after entry (written as either), for a limited or unlimited period, and lets its holder engage in any activity a business visa may be granted for (reg 10(4)); its fee is nil. Its work isn't written as `any`, since the regulation names business visa activities rather than work as such. A dependant's visa lets a dependant of a business or residence visa holder reside with them, for the rest of that visa's period, applied for before, on or after entry, at $1,000 (regs 7 and Table 2). No permanent residence, renewal or decision time is set in the Regulations, and naturalisation isn't read here. The lead took out the $6,000 written for the business visas (Employment, General) on 2026-10-30: the table's column it sits in wasn't identified, so the fee is left out until it is.
